item.title: The Proprietary Architecture of Mathematical Reasoning
item.description: OpenAI's retention of core mathematical scaffolding highlights a widening gap between open consumption and proprietary infrastructure, raising questions about reproducibility in automated reasoning. While commercial utility increases, independent verification of foundational claims remains constrained by architectural secrecy.

item.title: Former Professor Arrested After Months of Impeding Delivery Robots
item.description: A 78-year-old retired communications professor was arrested for disorderly conduct in Philadelphia after repeatedly standing in the path of autonomous delivery rovers. While framed as a civil protest against automated labor displacement, the incident highlights emerging legal collisions between pedestrian rights and commercial rights-of-way.

item.title: JAXA is about to perform a Phobos sample return mission
Guarding the Git Hook Against the Ghostwriter
item.description: A new developer tool intercepts commits to quiz engineers on AI-generated code before it reaches production, trading shipping speed for a sobering moment of forced comprehension.

item.title: Show HN: 500 clocks in one 6.3 MB HTML file by Opus 5.5
Voice cloning platforms codify the erosion of vocal authorship
item.description: Weights AI provides consumer tooling to map licensed voices onto arbitrary tracks, lowering the friction of imitation while quietly accelerating copyright erosion. The tradeoff is widespread cultural pastiche at the expense of legal and artistic provenance.

item.title: X11appjail v2.0.0 Prods at the Fragile Boundaries of Desktop Sandboxing
item.description: This release tests D-Bus proxying and Linux-brave isolation, navigating the eternal friction between system lockdown and desktop utility. The inherent risk is that tighter containment routinely shatters subtle inter-process assumptions.
